mesoscaleDiscussions.areas: Southern North Dakota into northeast South Dakota and far western Minnesota
mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: Elevated thunderstorms developing along the North Dakota/South Dakota border may continue to intensify and grow upscale over the coming hours. If upscale growth can occur, a more pronounced severe risk may emerge and require watch issuance. Convective trends are being monitored.

details.label: Areas affected
details.text: Southern North Dakota into northeast South Dakota and far western Minnesota

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Deep convection has begun to emerge along the ND/SD border over the past 30-45 minutes with additional towering, but weaker, convection noted in GOES IR imagery over southern and eastern ND. Similar to previous attempts at sustained deep convection, this activity appears to largely be driven by increasing isentropic ascent within the warm advection branch of a weak cyclone over the western Dakotas - augmented by a slight uptick in the nocturnal jet strength over the past hour (per regional VWPs). This emerging convection resides on the northern periphery of a buoyancy reservoir with MUCAPE values as high as 4000 J/kg analyzed downstream into SD. Additionally, 50-60 knot effective bulk shear was recently sampled by the 00 UTC BIS and ABR RAOBs, suggesting that intensification/organization of this convection is likely. Given the trends in IR imagery, adequate forcing for ascent, and downstream environment, it appears possible that some severe threat will emerge over the next few hours along the ND/SD border. Latest runs of the RRFS appear to be capturing convective trends well and suggest additional convection will manifest over the next 1-2 hours before growing upscale. If/when this occurs, the potential for severe hail and severe wind gusts will likely increase. Convective trends are being monitored, and watch issuance may be required if convective coverage increases.
